correctness.rationale: All generator domains are ℛ(ker(gh-I),im(gh-I)) and are preserved as rectangles under composition by a tensor-factor intersection argument. An F_q-line of matrices is idempotent type iff a nonzero rank-one generator squares to a nonzero multiple of itself; otherwise it is square-zero type. The rank-one projections and regular-nilpotent perturbations of identity explicitly realize every line isomorphism. The matrix-unit composition rule, minimal ideals, exact counts and properness witness follow. The provided prime-field checker exhaustively verifies individual conjugator generators for n=2,q=2,3 and n=3,q=2, with output VERIFY_OK. The infinite-dimensional/other-field cases are proved by algebra, not extrapolated.

value.rationale: This determines every minimal nonzero ideal, all their local groups and the exact order of the rank-one-plus-units skeleton in the concrete matrix endomorphism semigroup family of an explicitly posed open problem. The idempotent-versus-square-zero difference is intrinsic (trivial versus F_q^× isotropy) and the q^(d^2) domain filtration motivates the first layer. The theorem is structural for every n>=3 and every prime power, not a finite arbitrary slice; it explicitly does not purport to solve the full monoid classification.
